## Summary
- Switch `agent-self-approve.yml` from ACPX `approve-reads` to `approve-all` so the self-approval agent can run required read-only `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`, and `git fetch` investigation commands.
- Keep the workflow's GitHub permissions read-only for the agent job.
- Update the workflow contract regression test.

## Verification
- `npm --prefix .agent ci`
- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`

Fixes #328

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 189c12e9c4c090c89724a7979a72b618ea381427 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #329 fixes issue #328, where self-approval runs blocked because ACPX `approve-reads` does not allow shell-level inspection commands such as `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`, or `git fetch`.
- The PR changes `.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml` so the self-approval agent runs with `permission_mode: approve-all`.
- It keeps the `github_token` passed to the model step as the read-only `${{ github.token }}` and updates the workflow contract test to expect `approve-all`.
- The intent is sound, but the current implementation widens the model step inside the same job that later performs privileged deterministic approval resolution.

## Review
The reviewers agree that the docs are stale, but disagree on whether `approve-all` preserves the self-approval trust boundary. The synthesis treats the trust-boundary concern as blocking because the current workflow still runs privileged resolver steps from the same mutable checkout after the model step.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Self-approval agent can affect privileged resolver | BLOCKING | The changed [`permission_mode: approve-all`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/189c12e9c4c090c89724a7979a72b618ea381427/.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml#L137) lets the model run arbitrary shell/file operations before [`resolve-self-approve.js`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/189c12e9c4c090c89724a7979a72b618ea381427/.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml#L180) runs from the same checkout with the resolved Sepo auth token. |
| Self-approval permission docs are stale | WARNING | The workflow and test now say `approve-all`, but [`request-lifecycle.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/189c12e9c4c090c89724a7979a72b618ea381427/.agent/docs/architecture/request-lifecycle.md#L46) still lists `approve-reads`, and [`supported-workflows.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/189c12e9c4c090c89724a7979a72b618ea381427/.agent/docs/architecture/supported-workflows.md#L292) still says read-approved permissions. |

## Progress
- The PR already updates the workflow contract test for the literal `permission_mode` value.
- The workflow still passes `${{ github.token }}` to the agent step rather than `steps.auth.outputs.token`.
- Current PR checks show the `check` job passing; agent/cleanup jobs are skipped.
- No existing inline review comments or threads were present before synthesis; one inline comment was posted on `.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml` line 137 for the blocking trust-boundary issue.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Self-approval agent can affect privileged resolver</summary>

**Cause:** `runAcpx` inherits `process.env`, the job has `id-token: write`, and the model step now runs with `approve-all` before later privileged steps execute from the same workspace. That means prompt-influenced model execution can tamper with `.agent/dist/cli/resolve-self-approve.js`, affect `$GITHUB_PATH`/`$GITHUB_ENV`, or attempt the hosted OIDC exchange before resolver code uses the Sepo auth token.

**Candidate solutions:** Split model inspection into an unprivileged job with no OIDC/write-capable auth and run resolver code later from a fresh trusted checkout, or pre-gather the required PR context deterministically and keep the model on a non-mutating permission mode. Add/update the workflow contract test to assert the isolation boundary, not only the permission string.

**Comments:** One reviewer considered the read-only `github.token` sufficient, but the current same-job mutable workspace and inherited OIDC environment make that boundary incomplete.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Self-approval permission docs are stale</summary>

**Cause:** The PR changes the workflow permission mode without updating architecture docs that describe self-approval as `approve-reads` / read-approved.

**Candidate solutions:** Update `request-lifecycle.md` and `supported-workflows.md` to describe the final model after the trust-boundary fix, including the distinction between ACPX tool mode, read-scoped GitHub token, and deterministic resolver authority.

**Comments:** Both reviewers identified documentation drift; the exact wording should follow the final implementation choice.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: The unresolved blocker and docs drift require concrete branch changes, and an automated fix-pr pass can isolate the model inspection path while updating tests and docs.

## Final Verdict
`NEEDS_REWORK`

## Action Items
- [ ] Isolate model-driven self-approval inspection from privileged resolution so the `approve-all` agent step cannot use OIDC, mutate later resolver code, or affect privileged-step environment.
- [ ] Update the workflow contract regression test to assert the final isolation/trusted-runtime boundary.
- [ ] Update `.agent/docs/architecture/request-lifecycle.md` and `.agent/docs/architecture/supported-workflows.md` to match the final self-approval permission model.

No. The blocker is strict, but I think it is justified for **self-approval**.

The PR correctly keeps the agent’s explicit `github_token` as read-only, but `approve-all` gives the model shell/file-system authority in the same job before the privileged resolver runs. In the current workflow, the model step runs at `.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml#L127-L158`, then `resolve-self-approve.js` runs later from the same checkout with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.auth.outputs.token }}` at `#L163-L180`. Since `runAcpx` inherits the job environment, and the job has `id-token: write`, the agent is not isolated from later privileged execution.

The deterministic resolver has good checks: it rereads PR state, verifies trusted review provenance, checks actor separation, and requires matching head SHAs. But those checks only help if the resolver code and future step environment remain trusted after the model step. With `approve-all`, the agent could mutate files in `.agent/dist`, alter future step environment via `$GITHUB_ENV`/`$GITHUB_PATH`, or try the OIDC path directly. That is exactly the trust-boundary concern the review is flagging.

So my read is:

- **Blocking trust-boundary concern:** fair for this PR, because self-approval is a privileged governance path.
- **Docs drift:** real but should be warning/follow-up level unless the implementation changes.
- **The PR intent:** still sound. The fix should allow read-only investigation, but either isolate model inspection from privileged resolution, run resolver from a fresh trusted checkout/job, or pre-gather PR context deterministically and keep the model on a less permissive mode.

I would not treat the review as “too strict”; I would treat it as asking for the missing isolation around an otherwise reasonable `approve-all` direction.

- Kept the PR scope docs-only for this fix-pr pass; no workflow or resolver isolation changes were added.

## Rubrics Review

| Total Score | Verdict | Rubrics Scored |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 78 | PARTIAL | 6 |

| Dimension | Rubric | Result | Score | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| coding_workflow / generic | Keep Docs In Sync | pass | 7/7 | The PR updates `.agent/docs/architecture/request-lifecycle.md` and `.agent/docs/architecture/supported-workflows.md` to reflect `agent-self-approve` now using `approve-all` while still passing read-scoped `github.token`. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Reuse Existing Code | pass | 8/8 | The implementation changes the existing `run-agent-task` `permission_mode` input and existing workflow contract test instead of adding new command wrappers, parsers, or alternate inspection paths. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Make Surgical Changes | pass | 8/8 | The diff is narrowly scoped to one workflow setting, one matching test expectation, and two doc updates. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Separate Decision Gates From Action Authorization | partial | 5/8 | The deterministic resolver still owns approval submission and uses `steps.auth.outputs.token`, while the model step receives only `${{ github.token }}`. However, the judgment step now has `approve-all` in the same job before privileged resolution, so the action boundary relies on convention and token scoping rather than stronger execution isolation. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Keep Privileged Workflows On Trusted Runtime Code | partial | 4/8 | The workflow checks out the default branch, which is good, but `approve-all` lets the model step run shell/file operations before `node .agent/dist/cli/resolve-self-approve.js` executes from the same workspace with the resolved Sepo auth token. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Validate Preview Contracts | not applicable | N/A | This PR does not add or change a dry-run, preview, or read-only mode contract. |

## Notes

- The PR now satisfies the linked issue #328 acceptance criteria: `agent-self-approve.yml` switches the self-approval agent to `approve-all`, keeps the agent token read-scoped, and updates the contract test.
- The docs drift flagged in the earlier review is fixed in the current diff.
- The remaining rubric tension is the privileged workflow boundary: the maintainer explicitly asked to relax the prior blocker for now, but the relevant rubrics still score this as partial rather than full pass because model-controlled shell access runs before deterministic privileged resolution in the same job.

## Findings

- **WARNING:** Against the trusted-runtime and decision-gate rubrics, `approve-all` in the self-approval agent step weakens isolation from the later resolver. This is acceptable as a conscious product tradeoff if the project is relaxing the blocker, but it should not be counted as a full rubric pass.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PARTIAL

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: d136db985197a500147063df8019e2449f59bfb9 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #329 fixes issue #328, where the self-approval agent could not run required PR inspection commands such as `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`, and occasional `git fetch` under ACPX `approve-reads`.
- The PR switches [`agent-self-approve.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/d136db985197a500147063df8019e2449f59bfb9/.github/workflows/agent-self-approve.yml#L137) to `permission_mode: approve-all` while still passing the read-scoped `${{ github.token }}` to the model step.
- It updates the workflow contract test and the architecture docs so the documented self-approval permission model matches the implementation.
- A prior review flagged the same-job trust boundary as blocking, but the maintainer explicitly accepted relaxing that concern for now to allow `approve-all`.

## Review
The current review artifacts agree that the PR now satisfies the linked issue and that the earlier documentation drift is fixed. The remaining disagreement is severity: one reviewer recommends `SHIP`, while Codex and the rubrics review keep the self-approval isolation concern as a non-blocking warning.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Accepted self-approval isolation tradeoff | WARNING | `approve-all` lets the model run local shell/file operations before the privileged resolver runs in the same job. This remains a real hardening concern, but it is acknowledged and explicitly accepted for this PR. |
| Loose test wording around read-only behavior | INFO | The workflow contract test still describes the flow as read-only while now asserting `approve-all`; the important read-scoped `github_token` assertion remains present. |

## Progress
- The stale docs called out in the earlier synthesis are fixed in `request-lifecycle.md` and `supported-workflows.md`.
- The PR keeps the model step on `${{ github.token }}` rather than the privileged resolver token.
- Existing inline feedback already covers the line 137 trust-boundary concern, so no duplicate inline comment was posted.
- No thread was resolved or minimized; the existing thread is not viewer-resolvable, and the current synthesis treats the concern as accepted rather than fixed.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Accepted self-approval isolation tradeoff</summary>

**Cause:** The model step now has ACPX `approve-all` in the same job before `resolve-self-approve.js` runs with the resolved Sepo auth token.

**Candidate solutions:** Future hardening could split model inspection into a no-OIDC/read-only job and run resolution from a fresh trusted checkout, or pre-gather PR context deterministically and keep the model on a less permissive mode.

**Comments:** This was the main reviewer disagreement. The maintainer explicitly chose to accept the tradeoff for now, so it should not drive another automated fix-pr pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Loose test wording around read-only behavior</summary>

**Cause:** The test name still leans on “read-only” language even though the ACPX tool mode is now `approve-all`.

**Candidate solutions:** Optionally rename the test or add a narrow assertion that the model step does not receive `steps.auth.outputs.token`.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION`: No unresolved required branch-change work remains; the remaining concerns are accepted or optional follow-up hardening.

## Final Verdict
`SHIP`

- [ ] No required branch-change work remains.

No changes were committed to [`agent/rubrics`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/tree/agent/rubrics) from PR #329.
